profile.summary: ICEBERG predicts the tandem mass spectrum (MS/MS) of a molecule by simulating how it breaks apart in collision-induced dissociation. Given a molecular structure, collision energy and polarity, it generates plausible fragments and predicts their intensities, giving a spectrum. Its main use is ranking candidate structures for an unknown spectrum by how well their simulated spectra match.

summary_quotes.text: Here, we present a geometric deep learning model, ICEBERG, that simulates collision-induced dissociation in mass spectrometry to generate chemically plausible fragments and their relative intensities with awareness of collision energies and polarities.
We utilize ICEBERG predictions to facilitate structure elucidation by ranking a set of candidate structures based on the similarity between their predicted

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ICEBERG has two stages. ICEBERG-Generate builds a pruned fragmentation graph (a DAG) by learning which atoms break off, allowing up to three atom-breaking steps and six bond breakages; its training labels come from the MAGMa algorithm, which enumerates fragmentations and matches them to observed peaks. ICEBERG-Score takes the fragment graph, uses a GNN with instrument parameters to embed fragments and the parent molecule, and a set transformer to predict fragment intensities, which are merged into a spectrum. Version 2.0 added collision energy and polarity as inputs, contrastive fine-tuning and charge migration.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: ICEBERG 1.0 (Goldman et al., arXiv 2304.13136) is archived on the iceberg_1.0 branch; ICEBERG 2.0 (Wang et al. 2025) is on the iceberg_2.0 branch; the main branch holds ICEBERG 2.1, which the README calls about three times faster with official NIST'23 support, alongside the newer GLACIER model. Open MassSpecGym-trained ICEBERG 2.1 weights (msg_all and msg_simulation) are shared on Dropbox; NIST-trained weights are given only to NIST licence holders on request. ICEBERG 1.0 was evaluated on NPLIB1 and NIST20. A result should name the ICEBERG version and the training data of the weights.

sections.title: Use in the benchmark source
sections.body: MassSpecGym in the Wild (an existing source on this record) trained two ICEBERG models with the ms-pred code: a leakage-free one on the MassSpecGym training set and an adversarial one that also saw the test set, to show how synthetic spectra from a forward model can leak test information into MIST training. It also reports ICEBERG forward-model retrieval on the full MassSpecGym test split, imputing missing collision energies, and says MassSpecGym v1.5 releases officially retrained data-safe versions of ICEBERG and other components.

run_guide.summary: Install ms-pred with uv, get the open MassSpecGym ICEBERG weights, and run the PubChem elucidation demo notebook.
prerequisites: A GPU is optional; the README says CPU-only inference is feasible with cuda_devices: None.
The MassSpecGym-trained ICEBERG weights from the README's Dropbox link.

steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/coleygroup/ms-pred.git
cd ms-pred
git checkout --detach e2fc3a95022b585bc372f4e5b63ae3a2ca3b97c6
